newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: LASTORE shares in very quiet JSE debut.
newsitem.headline: LASTORE shares in very quiet JSE debut.

text.p: South African clothing and footwear retailer LA Retail Stores Ltd (LASTORE) debuted on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) on Monday at a strong premium to its issue price but soon slipped weaker in very thin trade.
Dealers said Cape-based LASTORE, which was listed in the industrial stores sector, first traded at 320 cents, some 59 percent above its issue price to institutions of 201 cents a share.
"The share had a good open as it is seen to have good growth prospects," said a stores analyst who asked not to be identified.
"It only has about 20 stores and has said it plans to move from a regional to national chain. Store expansion is the best kind of growth in the retail sector," the analyst said.

However, shares soon slipped off these top levels as interest in the share was very limited. Dealers said this was due to confusion over the listing method which saw LASTORE reverse list into the Ensign Ltd cash shell.
"Ensign was not a very tradeable share," a dealer said. But a 10-for-one share split on Monday was seen boosting LASTORE's tradeability.

The absence of a public share offering had also dampened activity, dealers said. The share offer ahead of the listing consisted of a private placing of 24 percent of the shares with institutions to raise 10.5 million rand.
By 1100 GMT shares were changing hands at 276 cents recovering from a worst level of 270 after only 25,000 shares changed hands in eight deals.
Analysts said they expected the share to creep back towards the 320 cent level in the near term amid solid future prospects.

In its prospectus, LASTORE forecast earnings per share rising to 19.2 cents in the year to August 31, 1997 compared to 15.4 cents the previous year. It has predicted a dividend of 6.27 cents this year.
